tagline: Along the top of the cliffs, or along the bottom.
intro: From the New York line at Alpine the parkway runs south along the top of the Palisades to the George Washington Bridge at Fort Lee, laid out as a road within a park. Below it, between the cliffs and the Hudson, Henry Hudson Drive keeps to the foot of the rock. It was built between 1912 and 1940, and it is the only road in New Jersey that passes under the bridge.
Quarrying once threatened the cliffs. In 1900 the two states set out to acquire them, and in 1933 John D. Rockefeller, a backer of the parkway, gave 700 acres along the top of the Palisades.

moments.title: State Line Lookout
moments.text: One of three overlooks reached from the parkway, set on the highest point of the Palisades cliffs at 532 feet.

moments.title: Kearney House, Alpine
moments.text: An old stone house by the river at Alpine, long called Cornwallis's headquarters, was Rachel Kearney's tavern after 1831 and a park police station in the 1920s.

moments.title: Fort Lee Historic Park
moments.text: On the bluff above Burdett's Landing stands a reconstruction of Washington's 1776 encampment, blockhouse and battery, with two overlooks on the bridge and Upper Manhattan.

practical: Commercial vehicles are barred from the parkway. In the cold-weather season, roughly December through April, Henry Hudson Drive closes to motor vehicles from Dyckman Hill Road north to the Alpine Approach Road.
